title: Baron: senses 2–4 are effects — only first-sense fiducia is faith’s proper act
source_text: LX. Sed quicquid de eo sit, postquam Robertus Baronius quatuor illas fiduciae acceptiones proposuit, ad quaestionem istam, An fiducia sit actus fidei? respondit duabus assertionibus: Prima est haec, fiducia secundo, tertio, aut quarto modo accepta, non est fidei actus, sed est effectum & consequens fidei: Secunda vero illius assertio sic habet, Fiducia primo modo accepta est verus & proprius Actus fidei salvificae actus, imo est praecipuus & specificus ejus actus. In Philosophia Theologis ancillante, Exercitatione tertia, Articulo 18.
pass_a_gloss: But however that may be, after Robert Baron proposed those four acceptations of trust, to that question, Is trust an act of faith? he answered with two assertions: The first is this, trust taken in the second, third, or fourth way is not an act of faith, but is an effect and consequent of faith: But his second assertion runs thus, Trust taken in the first way is a true and proper Act — the act of saving faith — nay it is its chief and specific act. In Philosophy the Handmaid of Theologians, third Exercise, Article 18.
pass_b_english: Baron on ‘Is fiducia an act of faith?’ — two assertions.
Senses 2–4: not faith’s act but faith’s effect/consequent.
Sense 1: true proper act of saving faith — even its chief specific act.
